name: Center for Remote Health Monitoring (Ryan McGinnis, PhD)
org: Wake Forest University School of Medicine (Atrium Health / Advocate Health)
role: Founding director, Center for Remote Patient and Participant Monitoring; Associate Professor of Biomedical Engineering
why: The center runs several remote studies built on Oura Rings. Its April 2026 Frontiers in Digital Health paper used over 6 months of Oura passive sensing in 182 young adults to find next day panic attack risk factors. The team is NC based and works on wearable digital biomarkers at health system scale.

name: Vital Coach medical student resiliency study (Dermot Phelan, MD, PhD)
org: Wake Forest University Health Sciences / Atrium Health Sanger Heart & Vascular Institute
why: The Vital Coach study (NCT07342673) ran January to May 2026 with first year medical students and used nightly PPG wearable data as its primary outcomes: nocturnal HRV (RMSSD), nocturnal resting heart rate, sleep duration and sleep consistency (SD of mid sleep time). That outcome set is very close to what Vybe measures against each person's own baseline.
why_now: The registry record was updated on 2026-07-28 after the study completed in May 2026, so the team is likely planning analysis and any follow up cohort now.

name: 4YouandMe Our Transitions study and open source study app framework (Sarah Goodday, PhD)
why: 4YouandMe builds open source study apps for wearable research cohorts. Its Our Transitions study (NCT07597915) gives participants an Oura Ring Gen 4 and a Fitbit Sense 2 and collects data from both through its study app for 6 to 9 months. Its iOS framework is public on GitHub and was updated in October 2026, and its own site lists an Open Band Challenge for an open firmware wristband, so it serves researchers and thinks about open wearable data.
why_now: Our Transitions was posted with a May 2026 start (record updated 2026-05-20) and the 4YouandMeiOS repository was pushed on 2026-10-02.
